content.key_idea: CAPA's capacity-augment workflow is a fixed pipeline of four one-time orchestration/qualification steps followed by a per-domain Drain/Config/Undrain loop that repeats until every FBR SDN control domain has been processed.
content.reading_order: left to right along the top row (Request network model through Invoke Qual()), then along the bottom row (Drain/Config/Undrain), following the loop-back arrow back to Drain() while domains remain.

summary: Figure 3 lays out CAPA's capacity-augment workflow as a two-row sequential procedure, despite being captioned a state machine. The top row runs once: Request network model, then Orchestrate purchase orders, Orchestrate installation instructions, and Invoke Qual() on newly connected links to validate them before use. Control then drops to the bottom row, which loops once per FBR SDN control domain still needing attention: Drain() takes a single domain out of service (checked for permission and fleetwide rate limits by the SDN proxy), Config() applies the change, and Undrain() restores it, after which the loop condition 'While FBR SDN control domains remain' sends control back to Drain() for the next domain. Every call in the loop goes through the regulation layer's rate-limited, concurrency-controlled APIs.
